changes: scripts/promote-dist.mjs validates and restores package.json bin targets on staging before old-dist eviction and rejects symlink escapes. runtime-environment-checks.ts now reports compiled-version truth, emits stable global-core contract markers, and renders host-shell remediation: POSIX commands on POSIX and cmd.exe-valid commands on Windows. The red and realpath regressions cover both platform contracts.
usage: Run npm --prefix packages/main run build, then proof-or-stop --version and proof-or-stop doctor. The red regression prints contract: global-cli-bin-target-restored; a healthy doctor run prints contract: global-core-realpath-pass.
expectedOutcome: A build keeps proof-or-stop runnable and prints contract: global-cli-bin-target-restored in its regression. Doctor reports the resolved global core and prints contract: global-core-realpath-pass, with POSIX- or cmd.exe-valid remediation when repair is needed.
actualTranscript: Focused verification passed: red-global-cli-exec-bit printed contract: global-cli-bin-target-restored and GREEN; global-core-realpath printed ok; the real doctor command exited 0 and printed contract: global-core-realpath-pass.
outcomeDiff: No difference from the expected outcome on the tested POSIX host; simulated Windows branches validate npm-shim semantics and exact cmd.exe remediation.
limitations: Doctor remains read-only and reports commands without changing host state. POSIX execute-bit assertions and chmod-denial injections do not apply on Windows; Windows instead validates the byte-identical Node entrypoint, npm-generated shim contract, symlink capability, and pre-eviction failure safety.
pitfalls: Executable validation must remain before old-dist eviction. Do not use lexical containment alone for symlink paths, universal POSIX mode assertions for Windows, host-specific selector paths, or POSIX shell syntax in Windows remediation.
